name: SWIFT Heist
blurb: Draft exercise based on the documented incident “SWIFT Heist” (CTID Attack Flow corpus). A financial crime involving the SWIFT banking network.

injects.title: Spearphishing Attachment
injects.text: Suspected that phishing emails were sent to employees at Bangladesh Bank which dropped malware.

injects.title: Exploit Public-Facing Application
injects.text: Suspected that attackers gained access by exploiting weakness in a new electronic payment system (real time gross settlement).

decision.prompt: Responders see this activity (Exploit Public-Facing Application). What do they do?

choices.label: Vulnerability scanning involves the automated or manual assessment of systems, applications, and networks to identify misconfigurations, unpatched software, or other security weaknesses.
choices.lesson: ATT&CK: Vulnerability scanning involves the automated or manual assessment of systems, applications, and networks to identify misconfigurations, unpatched software, or other security weaknesses. This mitigation applies to 1 behaviour(s) in this stage.

choices.label: Privileged Account Management focuses on implementing policies, controls, and tools to securely manage privileged accounts (e.g., SYSTEM, root, or administrative accounts).
choices.lesson: A partial fix: Privileged Account Management focuses on implementing policies, controls, and tools to securely manage privileged accounts (e.g., SYSTEM, root, or administrative accounts). It helps, but misses the primary control for this behaviour.

choices.label: Treat it as noise and continue business as usual.
choices.lesson: Early-stage activity is usually the last cheap moment to intervene; waiting converts a contained event into an incident.

injects.title: Valid Accounts
injects.text: Credentials stolen for SWIFT operator at Bangladesh Bank.

decision.prompt: Responders see this activity (Valid Accounts). What do they do?

injects.title: File Deletion
injects.text: Attackers deleted files associated with SWIFT software to prevent employees from seeing the SWIFT messages.

decision.prompt: Responders see this activity (File Deletion). What do they do?

injects.title: Disable or Modify Tools
injects.text: Attackers used malware to disable printer, which prevented SWIFT acknowledgement messages being printed out for manual review.
